doc: Case-study mapping sidecar (BUILD_PLAN I4). Frozen M0 law IR cannot gain the maps_to field, so this file maps each M0 law to the whitepaper §11 ids it bears on, and each checked hypothesis (results/M2/hypotheses.json) to the §11.6 obligation it discharges. M1 laws carry maps_to in their own IR. An empty list means the law is outside the §11 catalog; tools/casestudy.py lists such laws under laws_outside. Written at the I4 prereg, before the coverage table existed (the M0 outcomes were already known then). Changed after the I4 review: L_par_hdr_ssvh now maps to D1, as its own note always said it bears on D1 (reported in docs/iterations/I4.md).

notes.L_par_hdr_ssvh: Bears on D1: the Solidity commit path always writes sequencerSetVerifyHash = 0, while Go BatchHeaderV1.Bytes encodes the field, and the pinned Go legacy-replay path can produce a non-zero one (common/batch/batch_cache.go:1447-1472). So D1's 'Solidity ≡ Go except byte 0' holds only under ssvh = 0, the premise L_par_hdr_v0 and L_par_hdr_v1 carry. Mapped to D1, this REFUTED law makes D1 partial under the coverage rule.
notes.L_rt_go_v0: Go getters recover every field of the header Solidity commits: the decoding half of D1.
notes.L_rt_go_v2: As L_rt_go_v0, version 2 (D1 names v0/v1 layouts; v2 reuses the v1 wire format).
notes.L_par_hdr_v2: Reproduces O2 against Go's BatchHeaderV1.Bytes, which hard-codes byte 0 = 1. At the pinned commit the Go batch producer does build version-2 headers, by patching byte 0 of BatchHeaderV1.Bytes() and storing the aggregate at [57:89] (common/batch/batch_cache.go:1727-1731), so O2's 'no v2 encoder' clause no longer holds there; the law's comparison is with the v1 encoder only.
notes.L_tag_BVH: The obstruction is observed on chain (the v2 header carries the hash a v1 commit stored). Its Go consumer side only reads both headers back and compares with aggregateBlobHashes; that inequality is HOLON's comparison and holds once the chain side does. No Morph consumer decision is exercised.
notes.L_fact_Z: On chain, the no-blob and zero-blob commits produce the same committedBatches. Derivation (ParseBatch) rejects both batches, with different messages, and handles them the same way, so the consumer side observes no divergence and the law's bin is pending.
